title: Derivation script does not emit the shipped tables: packet_classes emits ALL catalog classes, shipped mode tables carry only email/streaming — the 'paste verbatim' claim is false
evidence:
Script: '    classes = dict(CLASS_BASE)  # mode remaps for class colors' then only email/streaming are overwritten, and emit does '        if classes:
            table["packet_classes"] = {cid: list(c) + [255] for cid, c in classes.items()}' — every catalog class is emitted. Docstring: '       paste the "modes" block into data/palette.json verbatim).'. Shipped table: '"packet_classes":  { "email": [96, 102, 118, 255], "streaming": [24, 52, 140, 255] }' (two entries), while epic-7-context.md in this same diff states 'Nine distinct packet silhouettes (circle, rounded-square, triangle, diamond, hexagon, pill, star, tiny-square, blob)'.
detail: classes starts as a full copy of CLASS_BASE (all packet_types.json entries, ~9 per the diff's own docs), so emit() outputs a packet_classes entry for every class; the shipped tables hold only the two remapped ones. Re-running the script and pasting verbatim does not reproduce the shipped file — the derivation record is not faithful.
recommended_fix: Emit only the classes the mode actually remaps (diff classes against CLASS_BASE before emitting), or regenerate and re-paste the tables so script output and shipped data match byte-for-byte.

title: derive_a11y_palettes.py: dead helpers scale_lum/mix, unused params (verify's tune, pair_list's mode), and a docstring promising a search the code never performs
evidence:
'def scale_lum(rgb, target_l):' and 'def mix(a, b, t):  # linear mix in 8-bit space' are defined and never called. 'def verify(mode, remap, classes, tune=True):' — tune never referenced. 'def pair_list(mode, remap, classes):' — mode never referenced in the body. Docstring step 4: '  4. Where a pair collides, search the mode-space remap: shift lightness
     (the axis that survives ALL three deficiencies) and nudge hue onto the' — but verify's own docstring says 'no silent auto-nudging: anchors are the canon; if a pair fails, HAND-TUNE the anchors above.'
detail: The header documents a numeric search over lightness/hue; the implementation hand-sets anchors and never searches. scale_lum/mix are leftover machinery for that unimplemented search. The doc header contradicts the code below it.
recommended_fix: Delete scale_lum, mix, and the unused tune/mode parameters; rewrite docstring step 4 to state anchors are hand-tuned against the verify report (no automated search).

title: parity.odin: the '// 16. pause — W8 pin' comment is orphaned above the new settings-panel scenario, detached from the pause scenario it documents
detail: The hunk inserted the 7.3 scenario between the pause scenario's header comment and its append block, so the '16. pause' comment now reads as documenting the settings-panel code. Misleading for anyone maintaining scenario numbering.
recommended_fix: Move the '// 16. pause — W8 pin ...' comment down so it directly precedes the input_parity_pause append, keeping the 7.3 comment with its own scenario.

title: Spec and PR body name different intent sets: Settings_Toggle/Panel_Navigate/Panel_Activate/Scale_Step vs Toggle_Settings/Settings_Navigate/Settings_Activate (Scale_Step dropped)
evidence: Spec: '- `app/input/types.odin` + `poll/controller/touch` -- new Intents (Settings_Toggle, Panel_Navigate, Panel_Activate, Scale_Step); mapped on all devices'. PR body: '- **Input parity by construction**: new intents (`Toggle_Settings`, `Settings_Navigate`, `Settings_Activate`) mapped across keyboard (S, arrows, Enter, Esc), controller (Y, D-pad, A, B), and touch (chip + row taps via the shared ui-press seam).'
detail: The two documents in the same diff disagree on the new intent names and count (four incl. Scale_Step vs three). One of them misdocuments the public input surface; app/ is outside this chunk so correctness of either cannot be confirmed here.
recommended_fix: Reconcile both documents against the actual app/input/types.odin enum names; state the full intent set (including the scale-step intent or its absence) identically in spec and PR body.

title: Reduced-motion pinned value contradicts itself across docs: spec says 'mid-envelope factor (e.g. 0.99)', PR body says 'full static width ... not an average'
evidence: Spec: '- Reduced-motion static value: a fixed mid-envelope factor (e.g. 0.99) — deterministic, golden-stable; packet motion/lane speeds stay (gameplay readouts, not effects).'. PR body: '- **Reduced-motion pins the pulse to full static width** (max legibility, deterministic + golden-stable), not an average — a constant ring reads better than a frozen mid-pulse.'
detail: 'Mid-envelope' and 'full static width, not an average' are different design decisions for the same pulse_read pin. A future maintainer editing the static factor cannot tell which is the ruling.
recommended_fix: Update the spec's Design Notes to the shipped ruling (full static width) or the PR body to the spec value; keep one canonical statement of the pinned factor.

title: palcheck oracle picks the 48-vs-40 threshold by testing whether a pair's first color equals a map token, not by pair identity
detail: The Python derivation carries an explicit per-pair threshold; the Odin oracle re-derives it from color equality. Any signal token that ever equals a map color (both alpha-255 quads) silently gets the looser 40 threshold. Works for today's tables; misclassifies on a future token edit — exactly the failure the oracle exists to catch.
recommended_fix: Tag each appended pair with its threshold (e.g. append a {pair, threshold} struct) instead of inferring it from pr[0]'s color value.

title: Spec's demo-verb syntax 'a11y <mode>[,<mode>]' is not implemented: the parser has no comma handling and errors on anything but the three exact sub-forms
evidence:
Spec: '- `harness/demo.odin` -- `a11y <mode>[,<mode>]` demo verb'. Parser: '+				return {}, fmt.tprintf("bad a11y (want: a11y palette <name> | a11y reduced | a11y scale <pct>): %s", line)' and the palette sub-switch ends '+				case:
+					return {}, fmt.tprintf("bad a11y palette (deutan|protan|tritan): %s", line)' — 'a11y palette deutan,reduced' is rejected.
detail: The spec advertises comma-combined modes in one directive; the parser accepts exactly one mode kind per line (combination is only possible via separate lines, which the spec syntax does not say). Doc overstates the verb.
recommended_fix: Fix the spec Code Map to describe the actual grammar (one of 'a11y palette <name>' / 'a11y reduced' / 'a11y scale <pct>' per line, combinable across lines), or implement the comma form.

title: _pr_body.md committed to the repository root as a tracked file
evidence:
diff --git a/_pr_body.md b/_pr_body.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5c74ba6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/_pr_body.md
detail: A 73-line PR description is committed at repo root as a permanent artifact. PR bodies belong in the forge, not the tree; it will drift from the actual PR text and clutter the root (no gitignore entry covers it either).
recommended_fix: Drop _pr_body.md from the commit (paste it into the PR description instead), or move it under the existing _bmad-output docs area if it must be tracked.
